picks.style: ancient greek chorus, lyre and frame drum, layered female voices, solemn, keening, building
picks.why: The Cithaeron ode — the exposed child with the golden brooch, and the Sphinx's inharmonious song.

picks.style: tragic chorus, aulos and low drums, massed voices with a lead, driving, incantatory, dark
picks.why: You came, you came, O winged creature — the Sphinx ode, built on repetition and mourning of mothers, mourning of maidens.

picks.style: solo tragic lament, single lyre, unaccompanied female voice, slow, raw, echoing
picks.why: Antigone over three bodies, asking what bird on the high branches will come to mourn with her.

picks.style: roman comic serenade, tibia pipes and lyre, tipsy tenor, swaying, mock-passionate, theatrical
picks.why: The serenade to the door-bolts — Plautus's famous drunken paraclausithyron, marked in the text as sung.

picks.style: latin patter song, hand drum and pipes, fast wry male vocal, brisk, streetwise, rattling
picks.why: The tour of Rome by vice — the Etrurian street, the Velabrum, the perjurers behind Castor's temple.

picks.style: comic lament, plucked lyre and clacking percussion, groaning bass voice, mock-tragic, lurching
picks.why: The pimp's catalogue of ailments, spleen to intestines, answered with the advice to take a walk.

picks.style: english hymn, chamber organ and viol, plain tenor, slow, questioning, devotional
picks.why: So many years I've seen the sun — the poem's anaphora and its refrain of unanswered questions.

picks.style: funeral hymn, low organ and cello, grave baritone, hushed, resolving, benedictory
picks.why: The close of the same poem into the epitaph: his name, reproach and praise, was Man.

picks.style: common-meter hymn, four-part voices and harmonium, sober, steady, austere
picks.why: Here from afar the finished height of holiness is seen — and the deserts that lie between.

picks.style: mock-heroic drawing-room ode, harpsichord and strings, arch male vocal, brisk, satirical, sparkling
picks.why: The burlesque ode in Johnson's voice — behold him as your very Scrub, 'tis I myself am Thrale's Entire.

picks.style: 18th century elegy, fortepiano and viola, soft tenor, slow, tender, valedictory
picks.why: No monument, no panegyric — only flowers strewn yearly and the wish that the turf lie easy.

picks.style: pindaric ode, baroque orchestra with trumpet, declamatory tenor, stately, rising
picks.why: Hail, father of the British stage — the Shakespeare strophe, Melpomene smiling over Avon.

picks.style: hellenistic bucolic hymn, single lyre and syrinx, warm tenor, slow, luminous, evening-lit
picks.why: Blessed are they who love and are loved in return, then the hymn to Hesperus asked to light a lover's way.

picks.style: pastoral idyll, syrinx and soft frame drum, bright male voice, unhurried, sunlit, dancing
picks.why: Spring thrice-longed-for, all things conceiving — then the boy who tries to snare Love with birdlime.

picks.style: greek bucolic song, kithara and pipes, gentle mid-range voice, lilting, wry, tender
picks.why: Cypris hands the infant Love to a herdsman to be taught song, and Love does the teaching instead.

picks.style: pastoral blank-verse setting, acoustic guitar and soft strings, warm narrating voice, unhurried, sunlit
picks.why: Only candidate, and a strong one: how pagan Greece peopled its hills with Apollo, Diana, naiads and Pan.

picks.style: stoic hymn, low drone and plucked lyre, steady male voice, austere, resolute, slow
picks.why: Only candidate, but it carries Cleanthes' prayer — lead me, O Zeus, that way I'll follow without fret or cavil.

picks.style: eastern european folk lament, solo violin and low male voice, sparse, minor key, resolute
picks.why: The hammer shivers glass but iron by its blows is forged — a whole philosophy of history in a couplet.
